summary:
ASTRALIS is an interactive prototype for exploring how launch-vehicle selection, mission targets and orbital manoeuvres fit together. It provides six represented launch-vehicle configurations and five mission profiles spanning low Earth orbit, Sun-synchronous orbit, medium Earth orbit, geostationary transfer orbit and lunar transfer. Users can choose a vehicle and mission, view stage and mission information, run a simplified ascent sequence, and issue basic prograde, retrograde, normal and anti-normal orbital manoeuvre commands.

The project aims to make space-mission architecture easier to explore by connecting decisions that are often taught separately. The current build is an educational prototype: its visuals, vehicle geometry, guidance and orbital calculations are still being refined and validated, and should not be treated as flight-qualified engineering predictions.
details:
How ASTRALIS Works

ASTRALIS is an interactive space mission design and simulation platform that brings launch vehicle configuration, mission planning and orbital operations into one environment.

Users can explore six launch vehicle configurations: Falcon 9, Atlas V 551, Delta IV Heavy, SLS Block 1, Ariane 5 ECA and ISRO's LVM3. They can select from five mission profiles, including Low Earth Orbit, Sun-Synchronous Orbit, Medium Earth Orbit, Geostationary Transfer Orbit and Lunar Transfer.

The prototype connects vehicle selection and mission targets to a launch sequence with simplified gravity-turn guidance and flight telemetry. It also includes orbital manoeuvre controls for prograde, retrograde and inclination changes, with delta-v and propellant tracking.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTRALIS aims to make space mission concepts easier to understand by showing how launch vehicle architecture, propulsion, mission objectives and orbital manoeuvres are interconnected. It is intended as an educational and exploratory tool for students and space enthusiasts interested in aerospace engineering and mission design.

Technology and Development

The project is developed using Unreal Engine 5.8.4 and C++. Unreal Engine provides the 3D environment and interactive interface, while custom C++ systems handle vehicle configuration, simulation logic, mission selection and orbital manoeuvre controls. Claude Code and ChatGPT were used as AI-assisted development tools for coding, debugging and technical assistance.

Creative Approach and Engineering Considerations

The central idea is to connect different phases of a space mission rather than presenting launch vehicles, orbital mechanics and spacecraft operations as separate experiences. The design considers vehicle staging, propulsion configuration, mission targets, mass and propellant, delta-v requirements and orbital states.

ASTRALIS is currently an educational prototype. Its simulation accuracy, vehicle models, physics and visual presentation require further testing and refinement. It is not intended for real-world flight planning or operational aerospace engineering.
